back_translation: Then I heard Him call out in a loud voice, saying, “Let the executioners of the city draw near, each with a weapon of slaughter in his hand.”

And behold, six men came from the direction of the Upper Gate that faces north, each with a shattering weapon in his hand; and among them was another man clothed in linen, with a scribe's writing-case at his waist. They came in and stood beside the bronze altar.

Then the glory of the God of Israel rose up from the cherub where it had been resting, to the threshold of the temple; and He called to the man clothed in linen who had the scribe's writing-case at his waist.
The LORD said to him, “Go throughout the city, throughout Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of those who sigh and groan over all the abominations committed in it.”
And I heard Him say to the others, “Follow him through the city and kill; do not let your eye spare, and do not have pity.

Kill the old men, the young men, the young women, the little children, and the women, but do not go near anyone who has the mark; and begin at My sanctuary.” So they began with the elders who were in front of the temple.
He said to them, “Defile the temple and fill the courts with the slain. Go out!” So they went out and killed throughout the city.
While they were killing, I was left alone; and I fell facedown to the ground and cried out, “Ah, Lord GOD, when You pour out Your wrath on Jerusalem, will You destroy the entire remnant of Israel?”

He said to me, “The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great; the land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of injustice, for they say, ‘The LORD has forsaken the land, and the LORD does not see.’
As for Me, My eye will not spare, and I will not have pity; I will bring their conduct down upon their own heads.”
And behold, the man clothed in linen with the writing-case at his waist reported back, saying, “I have done as You commanded me.”
